meta.purpose: Five events, defined before any analytics beacon is enabled, so that 'which page works' becomes a question with an answer.
meta.status: Client written in assets/js/analytics.js (inert by default); self-hosted collector written in server/collect.js. Nothing is transmitted on static GitHub Pages until a first-party host and privacy notice are live. See FLG-010.
principles: first-party only: the collector must live on a first-party host, not a third-party tracker
no cookie, no persistent user identifier, no IP logging
aggregate only: no per-visitor profile is stored
no Amazon data: nothing about what happens after the click is knowable from this site, and nothing is implied
meta.explicitly_out_of_scope: Reported orders, revenue and conversion rate. Those can only come from the Associates dashboard or the API, which this session cannot read. The campaign ledger starts empty and stays empty until authorised first-party reports exist.

events.name: page_view
events.answers: Which pages are reached at all

events.name: outbound_click
events.fires_when: A reader activates an outbound sponsored link to an Amazon product listing
events.answers: Which products and which pages earn the click
not_collected: anything after the click; the destination is Amazon's, not ours
events.note: The click is counted locally before navigation. It does not prove a purchase, a session, or a commission.

events.name: guide_open
events.fires_when: A reader opens a guide from the front page or guides index
events.answers: Which question-shaped guides attract actual readership
not_collected: scroll path, mouse movement, personal identifiers

events.name: search_query_referral
events.fires_when: A visitor arrives from a recognized search engine host
events.answers: Whether organic search referrals are landing on guides or product records

events.name: report_import
events.fires_when: An authorised first-party Associates report is manually imported into the campaign ledger
events.answers: Maintains a dated provenance trail for reported clicks and orders

collector_design.payload: the event name, page path, optional product ref, and date — nothing else
collector_design.retention: aggregate counts per day per event; retention policy must be published before enabling
collector_design.opt_out: Inert by default until privacy notice, retention policy, and consent stance are confirmed
collector_design.why_not_deployed: Deploying it requires a host that can run a process. GitHub Pages serves static files only, so there is nowhere for the collector to run natively. See S-14.

rules: a row is added only when the figure comes from an authorised first-party report
every row carries the date the figure was pulled and the report it came from
no projection, no forecast, no model output is permitted in this table
reported_orders is left blank until the Associates report provides it
